title: Highlight the guess

job.text: Here is an answer the AI gave on its own: "Our Q3 revenue was $412,000 across 1,208 orders, up 14% from Q2." Tap every claim the AI could only be guessing — the numbers it would have to calculate from data it was never given. Leave the parts it was simply handed.

rules.feedback: Too wide. The brand name, the quarter and the field labels aren't guesses — they were given. Flag only what the AI had to compute: a total, a count, a percentage.
rules.lesson: Not everything is a guess; aim at the computed claims.

rules.feedback: You spotted all three guesses. Every one is a number the AI would have to calculate from data it was never handed. Each needs a tool or a source. Next, you hand them off.
rules.lesson: A right-answer number without a tool is a guess.

rules.feedback: You let a guess through. "$412,000", "1,208 orders" and "up 14%" are all numbers the AI would have to calculate. It was handed none of the data to do that — every one of the three is a guess.
rules.lesson: Confident numbers are the guesses to catch.

hints.nudge: Which of these numbers would the AI have to calculate to know?
hints.gap: The brand name and the quarter were given to it — leave those. What's left is computed: a total, a count, a percentage.
hints.moves: The three guesses are the dollar total ($412,000), the order count (1,208) and the percent change (up 14%). Leave the labels and the quarter alone.

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: Read the confident paragraph and believe the numbers.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: Mark every computed number and get ready to route it to a tool.

template.plain: When the AI gives you numbers, ask yourself: was it handed the data to compute this, or is it guessing? Reply "Which of these numbers did you calculate versus look up?"
template.tech: For each figure in the answer, ask the model to label it calculated | retrieved | given, and treat every "calculated" one as unverified.

notes: ChatGPT: ask it to label each number "calculated" or "given" — it often admits it guessed.
Copilot in Excel: any number it states that isn't a cell or formula result is a guess.
A chat AI that can't run code: treat every total, count or percentage as unverified until a tool produces it; never accept "I checked, it's right."
